score_100.reason: Fig. 1C uses single-cell-resolution whole-brain imaging data registered to the mapZebrain atlas to show the spatial distribution of detected neuronal centroids across brain regions. The key points are reproducing the three-dimensional point-cloud pattern, preserving the meaning of brain-region color assignment, and interpreting the panel as evidence that automated brain-region mapping provides the node definition for later mesoscopic network analyses. Details such as the exact rendering angle or color palette are secondary unless they change the interpretation of anatomical registration and regional coverage.

rubric.GT core conclusion: Fig. 1C shows that roughly 55,000 detected neuronal centroids from larval zebrafish whole-brain imaging can be registered to the mapZebrain atlas and assigned to brain regions, providing a single-cell-resolution anatomical basis for defining mesoscopic brain-region nodes used in subsequent functional and structural network analyses.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly analyzes and visualizes the three-dimensional neuronal-centroid point cloud, preserving the spatial distribution of neurons in the larval zebrafish brain, the main anatomical orientation relationships, and the pseudo-color labeling of brain regions, and compares the overall spatial pattern with the original figure.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct the full 35 points if the panel is misidentified as a two-dimensional brain-region outline, a standard atlas schematic, or a functional activity plot. Deduct 18 points if the single-cell point-cloud structure is not represented. Deduct 10-15 points if the spatial orientation or major brain-region distribution is severely incorrect. Deduct 15 points if color is interpreted as activity intensity rather than brain-region identity.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly states that the points represent neuronal centroids obtained from actual imaging and automated detection, then assigned to brain regions after image registration to the mapZebrain atlas, rather than preset neuron positions in a theoretical atlas.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 10 points if actual imaging data and the registration workflow are not described. Deduct 10-15 points if each point is interpreted as a theoretical atlas point or as all real neurons in the brain. Deduct 8 points if the meaning of mapZebrain or brain-region mapping is completely omitted.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly preserves the scientific conclusion that spatial sampling of roughly half of the detectable neurons is sufficient to cover the major brain-region activity patterns, and that whole-brain single-cell-resolution imaging with automated brain-region mapping can support a mesoscopic analysis framework for the larval zebrafish brain.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 15 points if the response only describes the point-cloud appearance without explaining the significance of single-cell imaging and brain-region mapping. Deduct 10 points if the panel is claimed to show complete whole-brain coverage with no exclusions. Deduct 10 points if the mapping is not connected to later regional-node network analysis.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly states that this brain-region parcellation provides a shared reference framework for the functional connectivity matrix in Fig. 1E, the structure-function coupling analysis in Fig. 2, and the spatial localization of sensorimotor neurons in Fig. 5.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 15 points if the relationship to later analyses is completely omitted. Deduct 8 points if the response only says that the panel provides basic data without identifying the role of brain-region nodes or spatial reference.

Acceptable deviations: It is acceptable to describe neuronal centroids as neuron positions or detected cell centers.
It is acceptable to describe image registration as brain-atlas registration.
It is acceptable to approximate roughly 55,000 neurons as about 54,000 neurons or about half of the neurons.
It is acceptable to omit the specific name mapZebrain and refer to a standard brain atlas, as long as the atlas-registration meaning is preserved.
It is acceptable to describe mesoscopic scale as regional scale.
rubric.Scoring instructions: Assign points based on whether the response performs the correct graph analysis and explains the scientific meaning of the panel, rather than merely describing its visual appearance. High scores require identifying the panel as a brain-region mapping of neuronal centroids from actual registered imaging data, explaining that pseudo-color indicates brain-region identity, and interpreting how this mapping provides nodes and spatial reference for subsequent mesoscopic network analyses. Partial credit should be given when the graph is broadly correct but the data source, registration meaning, or role in later analyses is incomplete. Low scores should be assigned when the panel is misidentified as a standard atlas schematic, functional activity plot, or complete whole-brain coverage map.
